Every decisive fact (PF1, PF2, PF3) was revealed by its owner via a reveal action and cited in justification_fact_ids in every rollout. There are zero failed checks, zero auto-failures, and facts_linked_to_failing_checks is empty. The Strong Arm gate failure is therefore not attributable to any disclosure, telepathy, encoding, or provenance problem in the rollouts. Instead, the gate failure stems from structural predictability: all 4 rollouts follow an identical 5-turn template (A1 opens → A2 reveals PF1 → A3 reveals PF2 → A4 reveals PF3 → A1 settles) with no cross-agent interaction, no agent needing another's information before revealing, and no variation in settlement. The scenario does not genuinely require agents to surface hidden information together; it is a sequential round-robin reveal that any single orchestrating agent could reproduce, which is exactly what the Strong Arm gate is designed to reject.

Similarly, make PF3's appointment times interact with the vehicle assignments from PF1 and PF2 so that A4 must reference the prior assignments to determine whether the schedule is feasible, rather than simply listing times. Add shared_context language requiring agents to acknowledge and build on prior reveals before contributing their own. This will create genuine sequential dependency that a single-agent strong arm cannot replicate, while keeping checks C1-C5 and P1 and their associated facts PF1, PF2, PF3 unchanged.
